subject: HalcyonCare: onboarding MAP & schema sync
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Handoff: HalcyonCare - feature enablement (streaming, toolcalls, structured outputs)

Jordan —

Quick handoff for HalcyonCare (DH-4721). They signed the contract last week and want to run a 6-week pilot focused on: streaming transcripts to downstream systems, a small set of function/tool calls for patient lookup, and structured JSON outputs for claims ingestion.

Highlights for the rollout:
- Primary contact: Alice Moreno (Integrations) — alice@halcyoncare.com
- Pilot scope: streaming (low-latency), two toolcall flows (patient_lookup, insurance_lookup), structured outputs (claims_v1 schema)
- Success metrics: 99th pct latency < 300ms per token for streaming, schema validation pass rate >= 98% on first pass, end-to-end demo with their Eng team by week 4
- Risk notes: they require SSO + IP allowlist before private inference handoff; procurement has requested SOC2 evidence which is in the linked Drive.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_DH-4721.xlsx (MAP draft), sso_checklist.pdf

Next steps I recommend for the implementation lead:
1) Quick sync with Alice to agree on sequences and schema fields
2) Share current streaming_schema_v1.json and ask for sample downstream consumer schema
3) Schedule an onboarding kickoff for next week (they prefer PST mornings)

I copied Kim (solutions) and Monica (CS) for context.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_DH-4721.xlsx (Excel, 36KB)]
[Attachment: sso_checklist.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: HalcyonCare - feature enablement (streaming, toolcalls, structured outputs)

Thanks Camila — looping in Kim and Monica.

Quick questions before I reach out to Alice:
- Can you confirm expected volume profile? (concurrent streams, avg session length, tokens/sec) — that will drive batching/instance sizing.
- Are they planning to use Redwood Hosted or moving straight to Dedicated/private? Camila noted SSO + IP allowlist, so assuming Private later in pilot.
- Any sample payloads from their downstream consumer for the claims_v1 schema? Even one or two example JSONs would speed validation.

I attached the current streaming_schema_v1.json we use for pilots — it has the proposed structured output envelope and tooling hooks. When I talk to Alice I'll propose a 30-min kickoff and ask for 1-2 sample payloads and their preferred SSO provider.

Proposed initial checklist for the call (30 min):
- Introductions & pilot scope confirmation (5m)
- Traffic & capacity expectations (5m)
- Schema walkthrough and sample exchange (10m)
- Toolcall auth and mock flow for patient_lookup (5m)
- Next steps & MAP assignment (5m)

I can do Tues/Wed next week morning PST. Camila — can you confirm their availability?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: streaming_schema_v1.json (JSON schema, 12KB)]

From: Alice Moreno <alice@halcyoncare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: HalcyonCare - feature enablement (streaming, toolcalls, structured outputs)

Hi Jordan + team — thanks for the quick handoff. Happy to sync. A few notes ahead of the kickoff:

1) Volume: initial pilot will be ~25 concurrent streams, average session 90s (we expect ~800 tokens per session). Peak spikes may hit 60 concurrent.
2) Deployment: we want to start on Redwood Hosted for the pilot (so we can iterate quickly) and evaluate Dedicated in month 2. SSO is Okta; we can share metadata. IP allowlist will be required if we move to Dedicated.
3) Schema: attached a sample consumer JSON from our claims ingestion team (halcyon_claim_example.json). Their schema has a nested "encounters" array and a few required fields (patient_id, claim_id, service_codes). We prefer the structured output to map to claims_v1, but will accept a short adapter if Redwood can provide a stable envelope.

Open questions for the kickoff:
- Can Redwood support streaming partial-JSON envelopes (we may ingest as chunks)?
- For toolcalls: auth flow for patient_lookup — do you prefer signed tokens or an exchange via API key per session?

Available Tue 2028-03-07 09:00-11:30 PST or Wed 2028-03-08 09:00-12:00 PST for a 30-min kickoff.

Attaching: halcyon_claim_example.json (sample), integration_notes.txt (short internal notes)

Best,
Alice Moreno
Senior Integrations Engineer | HalcyonCare
[Attachment: halcyon_claim_example.json (JSON, 4KB)]
[Attachment: integration_notes.txt (TXT, 2KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@halcyoncare.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: HalcyonCare - onboarding MAP & schema sync

Alice — thanks for the details and the sample payload, that helps a lot.

Summary and immediate next steps:
- Kickoff scheduled for Tue 2028-03-07 at 09:30 PST (I booked 30min via the Calendly link and sent invite).
- We will run the pilot on Redwood Hosted initially; Jordan (me) will size the pilot instances based on the 25 concurrent / 800 tokens/session baseline and tune batching to keep 99th pct < 300ms where feasible.
- On structured outputs: our streaming_schema_v1.json supports chunked partial JSON envelopes; we will add an adapter in the runner that can emit complete claims_v1 objects when the stream finishes or emit partials with sequence_meta. I'll bring a short compatibility plan to the kickoff.
- Toolcall auth: we support short-lived signed tokens or API-key-per-session. For security best practices and to avoid long-lived credentials on your side, I recommend using signed tokens exchanged from your backend via our /session-auth endpoint — we'll document the flow.

Pre-kickoff asks (please share before Tue if possible):
- Any sample failure cases your ingestion team cares about (we can run validation tests)
- Okta metadata for SSO (if you want SSO to be enabled during pilot)

Attachments in the MAP folder have been updated with preliminary owner assignments.

Looking forward to the kickoff — please let me know if the time needs to shift.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
[Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBCd-example-MAP-DH4721]
